replication.target_description: Replication adaptation of perceived nationality in shared identity: French-English Frank, victory versus defeat, p. 7. N refers to the complete 2 × 2 nationality ANOVA supporting the simple effect.

n.sample_role: Participants in full 2 × 2 between-participants nationality ANOVA, including shared-identity simple effect.
n.exclusions: No participants excluded, including at manipulation checks.
n.location: p. 5 Participants and design; p. 7 Preliminary analyses / Replication of Stelzl et al.
n.quote:
The sample consisted of one hundred and fourteen physical education students ... All participants correctly reacted to the manipulation checks (i.e., double
nationality and tournament results). Consequently, no participant was excluded

from the analyses to be reported below.

notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical text: title Is Andy Murray More British Than Scottish? It Depends on His Success! Game Outcome and the MOATing Effect; authors Iouri Bernache-Assollant, Yves Chantal, Raphael Laurin (name encoding artifacts); DOI 10.1177/0033294120957242. Original Article, frozen author-uploaded full-text HTML parse with Methods, Results, Discussion, references and manuscript pagination 1–14; 2020 copyright matches assigned replication reference. No PDF supplied. Original source not inspected; unassigned original and other fields are placeholders only. The paper explicitly adapts the shared Canadian identity to French and the nationality outcome uniquely matches this description. Printed N=114 is explicitly retained for all reported analyses, not inferred from df. Mutually exclusive final groups reconcile 30 + 26 + 30 + 28 = 114. Shared-identity contributors: 30 + 26 = 56; shared-win cell n=30. These are distinct subgroup/cell roles, not the full critical-model N. ES, p and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
